key_insight: DeHNSSo-v2 extends nonlinear shear-flow stability analysis to compressible, body-fitted geometries while achieving approximately 10× speed-up on DeHNSSo-v1 nonlinear test cases.
engineering_relevance: The open-source solver supports boundary-layer transition and flow-control studies involving complex surfaces, resonators, and compressibility effects.
method: Compressible formulation with automatic grid generation and fourth-order curvilinear discretization.
Linear-cost sparse assembly and reusable per-mode factorizations.
Newton pseudo-arclength continuation for high-amplitude nonlinear solutions.
evidence_signal: Validation includes linear boundary-layer instability benchmarks at Mach 0.5–4.5, nonlinear oblique-mode breakdown at Mach 1.6, swept-wing crossflow against DNS, and resonator interactions against experimentally validated simulations.
watch_item: The reported speed-up applies to the tested DeHNSSo-v1 nonlinear cases; performance gains for other geometries and compressibility regimes require verification.
paper_title: DeHNSSo-v2: A compressible, curvilinear, and efficient extension of the Delft Harmonic Navier-Stokes Solver
